summary: A 132-anchor checkpoint lattice over episodes 1-1205, built from Detective Conan World's per-episode 'manga-source' field (V<vol> F<file>, plus absolute file numbers) converted to global chapter numbers with en-Wikipedia's volume lists (vols 1-108 = chapters 1-1154, continuous) and cross-checked episode-by-episode against ja-Wikipedia's 原作 column. DCW's own Manga Legend states File = chapter, and the identity was verified numerically at 627 of 631 manga episodes (the 4 residuals are case-span vs episode-span rows, not numbering errors), plus a 10/10 reverse check against DCW's Volume pages. Our episode numbering matches DCW's INTERNATIONAL column exactly across all 1207 rows (the Japanese broadcast count runs ~57 higher by ep 521 and was NOT used); air dates agree on 1196/1207 and every exception is a same-title row. The dominant structural fact is that Detective Conan adapts cases out of publication order - 201 of 631 manga episodes start below the running-maximum chapter - so END+1 is not a safe resume; continue_points are supplied for 80 anchors. Coverage through ep 1205 is chapters 1-1128 complete except chapter 594, which the TV series never animated. Our stored AFL types agree with DCW's manga-source on all 1207 rows (631 canon = manga, 569 filler = TV Original); the only residuals are 6 spinoff-adapting rows and Episode ZERO, all annotated rather than anchored.

structure.notes: ROW-COUNT IDENTITY - VERIFIED, NO SHIFT. Detective Conan World's season pages carry two numbering columns: the international episode number and the Japanese broadcast count (which inflates multi-part specials, e.g. our ep 521 = JP 570-571). OUR numbering matches DCW's INTERNATIONAL column 1:1 across all 1207 rows: air dates agree on 1196/1207 rows and all 11 exceptions are same-title rows where our stored air date is off by a week (eps 102, 110-115, 147, 353, 730, 904 - our 110/111/113/114/115 dates are scrambled among themselves, titles are in the right order). Title similarity is >=0.6 on 1168/1207 and every one of the 39 low-similarity rows is an alternate translation of the same title. No insert, no drift, at any point in 1-1207. FILE = CHAPTER. DCW's own Manga Legend defines 'File' as 'also known as chapter'. Verified numerically: DCW's V<n> F<k> label converts to the global chapter number via en-Wikipedia's volume lists (vols 1-108 = chapters 1-1154, fully continuous, no gaps) and agrees with DCW's own absolute file numbers on 627 of 631 manga episodes; the 4 apparent misses (eps 493, 494, 1185, 1205) are DCW rows where the parenthetical is the CASE span rather than the episode span, not numbering errors. Independent third check: DCW Volume pages' reverse {{ref anime|...}} mapping matched on 10/10 sampled anchors; ja-Wikipedia's 原作 column gives global File numbers directly and agrees with DCW on 621 of 632 manga episodes (the 11 exceptions are all grafts, parse artefacts, or per-case vs per-episode granularity - each is annotated). TYPE AGREEMENT IS PERFECT. Our stored AFL types and DCW's manga-source field agree on all 1207 rows: 631 canon rows all carry a mainline manga source, 569 filler rows are all 'TV Original', and the only 7 residuals are the 2 Detective Conan Special episodes (86, 113), the 4 Wild Police Story episodes (1029, 1038, 1042, 1061) and Episode ZERO (1187, already typed anime-only-canon). flags_for_sean: CONTINUE-POINT REGIME NEEDS A RULING. Because DC adapts out of order, the C2 'parity' continue point (first chapter not yet animated) is BELOW the episode's own END on 61 of the 80 continue_points emitted here (e.g. after ep 32, which adapts 105-107, the first un-animated chapter is 10). The alternative reading of C3 (furthest-covered + 1) would instead give a monotonic value. Each continue_point note carries BOTH numbers ('furthest chapter animated by this point: N') so either regime can be applied without re-research. If backward continue points are unacceptable to the UI, drop the continue_points block and keep the anchors.

Chapter 594 ('The Fugitive', V57 F8) is skipped by the TV series entirely (DCW Volume 57: {{ref special|Fugitive: Kogoro Mouri}}). Continue-point math here treats it as permanently skipped. If mangaMapper's model cannot express a permanent hole, ep-495-onward positions will read one chapter optimistic.

Both spinoffs have their own chapter space. They consume no mainline chapter, so they are left unanchored; if the interpolator treats an unanchored canon row as consuming mainline chapters it will over-advance across them.
